title: An additive equivalence of abelian categories carries injective resolutions to injective resolutions
statement: Let $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal B$ be abelian categories and $\Phi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ an additive functor that is an equivalence of categories. Then: (1) $\Phi$ carries injective objects to injective objects (and an object $I$ is injective iff $\Phi(I)$ is); (2) $\Phi$ preserves all limits and colimits that exist, in particular kernels and cokernels, and carries exact sequences to exact sequences; (3) consequently, if $s:X\to I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution of $X\in\mathcal A$ ($I^q=0$ for $q<0$, each $I^q$ injective, $0\to X\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$ exact), then $\Phi(s):\Phi(X)\to\Phi(I^\bullet)$ is an injective resolution of $\Phi(X)$; and a morphism of complexes $\varphi^\bullet:I^\bullet\to I'^\bullet$ lifting $\varphi:X\to X'$, or a homotopy between two such lifts, is carried by $\Phi$ to a morphism lifting $\Phi(\varphi)$, resp. a homotopy.

source.place: Homology, Lemma Tag 015Z (label lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives: a right adjoint of an exact functor preserves injectives; applied to the equivalence and its quasi-inverse), as used in Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 03YU (sites-cohomology.tex, label lemma-cohomology-bigger-site)
